text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • LynxCorp dedicated pool (eu2) - p99 latency breach
Severity: Sev2 -> Customer-facing SLO breach (p99 > 2x target)
Detected by: latency-monitor / route: /v1/generate (text-gen)
Link: https://inbox.redwood/incident/1769999999 • runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-pool-latency.md

mona: taking lead. Oncall acked. Paging runtime + SRE + CS.

Devon: on it — pulling per-tenant metrics now. Early signal: p95 ~1.3x baseline, p99 ~2.6x. CPU on pool nodes at 92%, GPU util high on 3 of 4 nodes.

Samir: seeing sustained long tail — KV cache miss rate jumped to 78% for this pool. Many requests with seq_len ~4k and heavy rerank batch sizes. Could be one tenant spiking.

Remy: 👀 I'm opening a comms thread with Lynx PS, notifying them of impact and asking for any known traffic changes. Will paste what they say.

ops-bot: ALERT • autoscaler didn't add nodes: quota_exhausted (account quota for eu2-dedicated GPUs reached).

Lee: quick model-level check: dominant model is open-llm-large-v2 (fp16). We have a quantized variant (open-llm-large-v2-q4) ready in the catalog. Fallback could reduce GPU memory pressure and speedup, but needs testing for quality.

mona: triage summary so far — region eu2, pool lynx-enterprise-eu2, likely tenant "lynx-search" causing bursty rerank traffic. Impacting generation latency for all tenants on pool (no isolation). Options: 1) tenant isolation (evict/buffer), 2) route tenant to lower-cost fallback nodes, 3) bump pool capacity (blocked by quota), 4) apply per-tenant rate-limit.

Devon: I can run an immediate soft-eviction for the suspected tenant to reduce interference. We have warm spare nodes in eu1; could we route them there for that tenant? Need handoff with networking (VPC) to ensure egress policies.

Samir: stepwise mitigation proposal —
1) apply temporary per-tenant throttle for lynx-search (drop or 429 above X rps)
2) soft-evict long-running requests for that tenant (graceful cancel)
3) switch tenant routing to fallback pool in eu1 (warm spare)
4) promote q4 quantized variant for non-critical routes to reduce load

mona: agree. Let's do 1 then 2. Remy — can you tell Lynx we will throttle their background rerank jobs for 30m and are moving to fallback nodes? Need explicit Ack.

Remy: pinged Lynx PS — they confirm an internal batch reindex started ~07:08Z and they didn't expect it to hit production endpoints. Asking to pause.

Devon: executing commands now:
```bash
# throttle tenant to 10 rps
redwoodctl tenants rate-limit set --tenant lynx-search --pool lynx-enterprise-eu2 --rps 10 --duration 30m
# check result
redwoodctl pool metrics --pool lynx-enterprise-eu2 --metric p99 --window 5m
```
Output: applied rate-limit -> p99 dropped from 2.6x to 1.9x within 90s. CPU still high but falling.

ops-bot: ACTION LOGGED • rate-limit applied by Devon (mona).

Samir: initiating soft-evict for active long-running requests for tenant (cancel with graceful fallback):
```bash
redwoodctl requests cancel --tenant lynx-search --pool lynx-enterprise-eu2 --filter "seq_len>2000 OR duration>15s" --grace 5s
```
Observed ~120 active requests cancelled (mostly rerank). Latency p99 improved to ~1.5x baseline.

Lee: rolling canary of quantized model for background routes now (non-chat) — patching routing policy to prefer q4 for route /v1/rerank-background for all tenants in pool.

mona: good. Next: evicting tenant to warm spare eu1 requires VPC routing change. Aisha, Julie - can infra confirm we have network path and IAM to route Lynx tenant to eu1 warm nodes? Also check data residency constraints with PS.

Aisha: infra confirms warm spare in eu1 available and uses the same VPC peering config for Lynx (pre-approved). No extra IAM changes required. We can flip routing via service-route config.

Devon: flipping routing (dry-run then commit):
```bash
redwoodctl routing set --tenant lynx-search --from-pool lynx-enterprise-eu2 --to-pool lynx-enterprise-eu1-warm --drain 10s
```
Committed. Initial traffic shows successful handoff with 0 auth errors. p99 for pool eu2 further dropped to ~1.2x baseline.

Remy: Lynx PS confirms they paused the reindex and appreciate the quick mitigation. They've asked for a timeline and RCA. I'll draft immediate customer note and share.

mona: outstanding: quota issue blocking autoscale — need followup with finance/quotas to increase burst GPU quota for Lynx account in eu2. Also need to run postmortem to consider tenant isolation rules.

Samir: logging snapshot for RCA attached (snippet):
```
[1769999999] pool=lynx-enterprise-eu2 node=gpu-3 kv_cache_miss=78% long_requests=314 p99=2.6x
[1769999960] tenant=lynx-search background_reindex=started rps=420 avg_seq_len=3800
```

mona: handoff — I'm going offline in 8m. Julie you're next oncall. Please continue with:
- validate autoscale quota request (ticket #INC-1769999999-QUOTA)
- coordinate with PS to confirm mitigations and ETA for final handoff
- start postmortem doc and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml for quantization fallback policy review

Julie: acked, taking over. I'll update the incident channel in 5m after confirming quota ticket.

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE • mitigation steps applied: tenant throttle, soft-evict, routing to warm spare, q4 canary. Current status: degraded -> recovering.

mona: thanks everyone. Post-incident tasks:
- Remy: send customer summary and next steps (within 30m)
- Devon/Samir: create follow-up to implement proactive tenant isolation thresholds (auto-evict or reserve capacity)
- Lee: expand model-variant playbook and run synthetic quality checks for q4 fallback
- Julie: own postmortem and SLA impact calc (p99 windows, uptime hit)

Julie: starting postmortem doc now — assigning to eng-runtime, eng-ml, SRE. Will schedule war-room follow-up.

Remy: customer note drafted and sent. Lynx appreciates the quick mitigation; they requested a scheduled call for a written RCA tomorrow.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigations active) • final status: p99 within SLO after routing and throttles. Postmortem required.

mona: closing thread. Thanks team.
